Subject: Request: operational exception for edge peering / latency attribution

Hi Vanessa / Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, EdgeCorp is implementing a customer‑managed edge peering layer in front of Redwood Private (our VPC). We’re requesting a formal exception in the SLA that attributes latency and short, transient outages to the customer‑managed network when the root cause is within our edge fabric.

Attached is a short network diagram (edge‑infra network diagram.pdf) and a timeline of the most recent incidents. The symptoms are identical to the examples you showed in the onboarding session — intermittent 200–800 ms spikes affecting inference calls during BGP flap windows.

What we need from Redwood:
- A clear carveout clause you can accept that excludes customer‑controlled edge peering from uptime/latency SLOs when verified by mutually agreed evidence.
- A repeatable evidence checklist (logs, traceroutes, peering flaps, timestamps) so we can expedite triage and avoid finger pointing.
- Commitment that the exception won’t block our ability to apply for Dedicated / Private tier upgrades if we meet other criteria.

We’re on a tight procurement timeline (deadline Nov 30) so any draft language you can share this week would be great.

Thanks — attaching the diagram.

— Alice
Alice Morton
Head of SRE, EdgeCorp

Hi Alice — thanks for the diagram and the clear ask. I’ve looped in Naomi (account lead) and Marcus (runtime/serving) so we can scope the technical and commercial side. Priyom from Legal is also on copy to help draft the carveout language.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- We can accept a narrowly scoped exception for customer‑managed edge peering where the root cause is demonstrably in the customer network and not in Redwood’s serving or control plane.
- We’ll propose a checklist for evidence. Typical items we’ll need: 1) time‑aligned traceroutes from an affected client to Redwood, 2) BGP flap logs from your peering fabric, and 3) request/response traces showing elevated server‑side queueing vs egress latency.
- Acceptance of the exception will be limited to the Private deployment tied to the specific account/region and won’t, by itself, preclude upgrades. We’ll add language to make the exception conditional on the documented evidence process.

I’ve attached an internal draft you can review — it includes a short fallback workflow and escalation path (proposed-sla-exception-draft.docx). Please confirm if EdgeCorp can provide the logs above and whether you’re open to adding a short retention window for evidence (30 days) for incident verification.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30‑minute technical sync with Marcus and your SREs tomorrow.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Alice — I reviewed the draft and proposed a narrower legal carveout and an evidence checklist. See the high‑level suggestions below (I attached a standard carveout template for reference):

Proposed carveout headliner (suggested wording):
"Redwood shall not be responsible for SLA compliance for latency or availability impacts where the demonstrable proximate cause of such impact is the Customer‑managed network layer (including but not limited to customer‑managed edge peering, transit provider outages, or customer‑operated load balancers), provided the Customer submits the evidence set described in the Evidence Checklist within 30 days of the incident.

Evidence Checklist (minimum):
- Timestamped traceroute(s) from affected client(s) to Redwood edge showing clear asymmetry or hops that indicate customer network latency.
- BGP session logs / message history showing flaps or route changes corresponding to the incident window.
- Application request/response traces with request IDs and server‑side timing demonstrating absence of server queueing or errors.
- Network device syslogs when applicable and available.

Operational notes:
- Evidence must be time‑synchronized (NTP) and delivered in a machine‑readable format.
- Redwood reserves the right to request additional telemetry if needed to validate root cause.
- If root cause cannot be established through the checklist, standard SLA processes apply.

I also recommend we set a monitoring instrumentation requirement as a condition of the exception: basic distributed tracing or request IDs preserved across the customer edge to Redwood (sampled at 1% min), so our teams can correlate requests quickly. Marcus — can your team provide a short spec for what we’ll need from the runtime side (headers, trace IDs, sampling)?

Alice — if you can confirm EdgeCorp can supply the items in the checklist (and accept the 30‑day rolling preservation window), Legal can prepare a short amendment for signature. I’ve attached the template: redwood-carveout-template.docx.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Alice — quick follow from engineering. We can accept the carveout as drafted, provided EdgeCorp implements either:

1) Pass‑through request IDs (X-Redwood-ReqId) populated at the client side and preserved through your edge, or
2) If that’s not feasible, a light instrumentation agent on the egress nodes that emits request-level timestamps (sampled).

Minimum sampling for useful correlation: 1% sampled requests with consistent request IDs and NTP‑synced timestamps. The agent/tracing requirement is an operational precondition for exception approval — without request‑level correlation we cannot reliably attribute latency.

Once EdgeCorp confirms which of the two options you’ll adopt and that the evidence retention window is acceptable, Legal can prepare an amendment (DocuSign link to follow). Happy to run a short tech session to finalize the headers and traceroute format.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
